Under the Financial Consumer Protection Act and its enforcement regulations, the items that must be explained by product type are specified as below (Act Article 19(1)).

Product type / Explanation items / Legal basis

- Protection-type (insurance) products:
  ① Product content: risk coverage, premium payment period, refund upon surrender or maturity, etc.
  ② Premium (including mutual-aid fee)
  ③ Grounds for limiting insurance payouts and payout procedure
  ④ Scope and period of risk coverage
  ⑤ Matters on contract cancellation and invalidity
  ⑥ Termination of contract by a direct seller due to violation of duty of disclosure/notification (Enforcement Decree (draft) Art.13(2))
  ⑦ Right to request premium reduction
  ⑧ Ancillary costs such as service fees
  Legal basis: Act Art.19(1)1(a); Enforcement Decree (draft) Art.13(2)

- Investment-type products:
  ① Product content such as operating period, costs, returns
  ② Investment risks (including scenarios in which maximum loss may occur and estimated losses)
  ③ Risk grade set by the direct seller (excluding linked investment contracts and non-monetary trust contracts)
  ④ Ancillary costs such as service fees
  ⑤ Matters on rescission/termination of contract (including disadvantages on termination)
  Legal basis: Act Art.19(1)1(b); Enforcement Decree (draft) Art.13(3)–(7)

- Deposit-type products:
  ① Product content: contract period, timing of interest/return payments and limitations on payments
  ② Interest rate/return rate and the basis for calculation
  ③ Ancillary costs such as service fees
  ④ Disadvantages upon termination
  ⑤ Important restrictions on use of the product such as account transfer limits
  Legal basis: Act Art.19(1)1(c); Enforcement Decree (draft) Art.13(8)–(9)

- Loan-type products:
  ① Product content: contract period, interest rate and calculation basis, whether rates are fixed/variable, whether prepayment fees apply, the applicable period and rate, etc.
  ② Repayment amount, interest rate, and timing by repayment method
  ③ Matters on creation of collateral rights (e.g., mortgages), grounds for enforcement, and changes in rights upon enforcement
  ④ Amounts borne by the consumer at contract (principal/interest, fees, etc.)
  ⑤ Disadvantages upon termination
  ⑥ Impact on credit score
  ⑦ Interest rate and disadvantages applicable in case of delinquency
  ⑧ Restrictions on use of the product such as refusal of contract extension
  Legal basis: Act Art.19(1)1(d); Enforcement Decree (draft) Art.13(10)–(11)

Note: Regardless of product type, items such as matters related to products/services linked to the recommended product, and the general financial consumer’s right to withdraw and to terminate unlawful contracts must also be explained (Act Art.19(1)2–4; Enforcement Decree (draft) Art.13(12)–(13)).

Chapter 3 Advertising Guidelines

Article 20 (Advertising copy and display methods)
① When advertising, the company must make the contents of Article 18 of these regulations easily recognizable to the general public and must comply with the display standards under Enforcement Decree Articles 6‑2 and 6‑3 of the Money‑Lending Business Act and Article 22(2) of the Financial Consumer Protection Act.
② When advertising under the preceding paragraph, the color/size of text or the speed/volume of audio must be composed so that benefits and disadvantages to consumers are conveyed in a balanced manner.
③ For banner ads, except where the advertising area is excessively limited, the company name and product name must be stated within the ad itself, not only on the linked online page.

Article 21 (Prohibited acts)
① When advertising, the company must not engage in the following acts that may mislead the judgment of loan consumers by using false/exaggerated expressions or unfair comparative displays, nor cause others to do so.

1. Advertising loan terms such as interest rates by the following methods:
   a. Advertising in a way that differs from the facts or exaggerates the facts
   b. Concealing or minimizing the facts
   c. Failing to specify the comparison target and criteria, or comparing with other financial products without objective grounds, or claiming superiority over other companies
   d. Providing definitive judgments on uncertain matters or statements likely to mislead consumers into believing something is certain
   e. Misstating or ambiguously stating matters that materially affect contract conclusion or the consumer’s rights/obligations (new as of 2021‑04‑00)
   f. Displaying loan interest on a daily basis so that the loan appears cheaper than it is
   g. Making it appear that terms that may vary by consumer apply to everyone
   h. Failing to clearly disclose the range/calculation method of loan interest rates, timing of payment/assessment, or ancillary benefits/costs, thereby causing misunderstanding

2. In ads related to loan products, emphasizing the name of the advertising medium or the name of a loan intermediary in a way that obstructs consumers from correctly recognizing the loan company.

② When advertising, the company must display in the following ways so that customers do not misunderstand the loan interest rate.

a. Display as “up to O% per year” based on the maximum interest rate. If displayed as a range (e.g., “O%–O% per year”), the specific qualification requirements for applying a particular rate must also be shown.

b. When displaying an interest‑free event, use wording such as “loan interest waived for O days,” and also show the specific qualification requirements for the waiver.

c. The delinquent interest rate must be displayed within the statutory maximum interest rate, as “contracted interest rate + up to 3%p.”

③ When conducting advertisements, the company must not use the following content:

1. Phrases that falsely imply anyone can get a loan
2. Names or phrases that could be mistaken for a credit financial institution or its affiliate
3. Phrases that encourage or may encourage indiscriminate borrowing or irrational consumption
4. Phrases that visually provoke disgust
5. Phrases that explicitly evoke sexuality or are excessively revealing
6. Phrases that glorify or encourage violence visually
7. Other advertising phrases specified by detailed rules when necessary to protect the company’s counterparties or prevent illegal transactions

④ When running video ads on terrestrial or cable TV, the company must not:

1. Run video ads on children’s or youth channels
2. Run video ads during the time slots specified in Article 9(5) of the Money‑Lending Business Act

⑤ When advertising, the company must not advertise on the following media:

1. Gambling‑specialized newspapers or magazines
2. Entertainment/sex‑industry specialized newspapers or magazines
3. Media targeted at children and youth

Article 22 (Inspection of advertising status)
① To verify the appropriateness of advertising conducted by the company, the committee may have the association’s responsible department inspect compliance with these regulations and with advertising review results.

c. Matters related to advertising content and methods

When advertising, not only the Financial Consumer Protection Act but also other laws such as the Act on Fair Labeling and Advertising, the Broadcasting Act, and the Money-Lending Business Act must be checked to avoid violations.

* Financial Consumer Protection Act Article 6 (relationship with other laws): Unless otherwise specially provided by other laws concerning financial consumer protection, matters are governed by this Act.

In particular, for online media such as YouTube and blogs, advertisers should comply with the Fair Trade Commission’s revised “Guidelines on the Display and Advertising of Recommendations/Endorsements” to prevent hidden advertising (e.g., when celebrities advertise without disclosing economic ties with the advertiser).

Items that must be included in ads under the Financial Consumer Protection Act can be operated flexibly within the limits of the regulatory intent, considering the purpose and characteristics of the advertising medium. Because advertising is not the contract stage, it is not necessary to explain products in the same detail as the duty to explain; however, information should not be omitted arbitrarily in a way that may cause consumer misunderstanding.

For online banner and pop‑up ads where the advertising area is limited, it is possible to split and post advertising content across linked web pages.

Items mandated by statute (e.g., Financial Consumer Protection Act Art.22(3)1–3) cannot be omitted from advertisements.

The Financial Consumer Protection Act provides broad discretion regarding advertising methods (text, video, audio), but requires that the color/size of text and the speed/volume of audio be composed so that benefits and disadvantages are conveyed in a balanced manner.

Financial product sellers should reflect advertising standards in internal control standards, referencing association review criteria and cited cases. Associations can report violations discovered during pre‑review to the Financial Services Commission.
